first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A planning service that will match me with an 'advisor' to plan a wedding somewhere in Portugal, Sintra palaces through to Algarve cliffs. The hero is mostly legal and weather facts, not what they actually charge or do. No price anywhere above the fold, which on my other tabs is the first thing I see.

attention_map.quote: Foreign couples start the legal process for a wedding in Portugal at least one month before the date.
attention_map.why: Plain facts, no 'dream wedding' fluff. That buys a bit of goodwill. But there is no price and no sign of what this company has actually done.

attention_map.quote: Legal and travel details from official sources, including IRN, GOV.UK and Smartraveller.
attention_map.why: Named sources I can check. More than the marketplaces bother with.

attention_map.section: Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue
attention_map.quote: The legacy of Ferdinand II, the King-Artist: a coloured, castle-like palace crowning the Sintra hills
attention_map.why: Tourist brochure stuff. Not what I am here for. The Monserrate roof works caveat was useful though.

attention_map.section: Choose Your Region / Booking a Sintra Palace
attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra; nothing may be fixed to the heritage. We check the terms with you before you book.
attention_map.why: Admitting a downside is rare and I trust it. But 'we check the terms' is not the same as telling me what happens if the state cancels me two weeks out.

attention_map.section: See Why Couples Marry in Portugal
attention_map.quote: a destination wedding in Portugal gives couples five things in one country.
attention_map.why: Repeats what I just read in the region cards. Filler.

attention_map.section: What Your Wedded Advisor Checks in Every Venue Contract
attention_map.quote: Buy-out or venue fee: a buy-out is often charged separately from the venue fee. ... VAT: whether each quote includes VAT, so totals compare like for like.
attention_map.why: This is the most useful box on the page for me. It names the exact places hidden costs live. Shame it stops at naming them and never puts a number on anything.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding, Step by Step: Getting there, Entry rules, Marrying legally
attention_map.quote: Legal and travel details checked October 2026, with official sources named.
attention_map.why: Thorough, dated and sourced by passport. I would bookmark this as a reference. It tells me they know the paperwork, not that they know the venues.

attention_map.section: What a Wedding in Portugal Costs
attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things: your guest count, the region, the season, how many nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use. We talk you through the options for your plans.
attention_map.why: A heading that promises costs and then gives zero numbers. Not even a range. That is the classic 'call us for pricing', which in my experience means expensive.

attention_map.section: See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes
attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package: every weekend is built to your plan ... and it can include: ... An on-the-day coordinator
attention_map.why: 'Can include' is not 'includes'. The heading says 'Includes' and the list is a menu of maybes. So is the coordinator extra? I can not tell what is in and what is out.

attention_map.section: Bring Your Guests, or Keep It Exclusive to You
attention_map.quote: Build a guest website in Wonderland Studio ... Start for free
attention_map.why: Out of nowhere. What is Wonderland Studio? 'Start for free' means there is a paid version. Feels like an upsell bolted into the middle of a wedding page.

attention_map.section: Celebrate More Than a Wedding in Portugal
attention_map.quote: Renew your vows on an Algarve clifftop above the Atlantic.
attention_map.why: Not relevant to me and a lot of scrolling.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding with One Wedded Advisor
attention_map.quote: Wedded Privileges. When you plan with Wedded Concierge, your advisor explains what the programme offers for your dates.
attention_map.why: This tells me nothing. What programme? What do I get? And the page never says what the advisor costs me. Free? A fee? A cut from the venue? That is my hidden cost question right there.

attention_map.quote: 4. How Much Is an Average Wedding in Portugal? There is no single average
attention_map.why: Same dodge as the costs card, word for word. The legal FAQs are solid and match the body copy.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding / Ronaldo and Georgina's intimate Portugal wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links, Ronaldo listed twice, under a label that reads like nobody finished the page. This is the only 'wedding stories' content on the page and none of it is a wedding this team ran. Looks cheap next to the careful legal section.

questions_answered.question: What is NOT included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: There is no from price anywhere. 'What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things' and 'There is no single average'. The contract checklist names buy-out, per-guest minimums, unfilled rooms and VAT as places costs hide, which helps, but there is nothing to compare against my other tabs.

questions_answered.question: Are these facts consistent across the page?
questions_answered.evidence: I checked: 'five regions ... served by four airports' matches the five region cards and LIS, OPO, FAO, FNC. 'Five heritage venues' matches the list of Monserrate, Pena, Queluz, National Palace of Sintra and the Equestrian school. 'At least one month' and 'within six months' repeat the same way in hero, steps and FAQ. Monserrate roof works 'until the first quarter of 2027' is the same in three places. Small wobble: the weekend list says 'civil, Catholic or symbolic' while the legal section's three forms are 'civil, Catholic, or civil marriage in religious form'. And the Azores turn up in honeymoon copy but are not one of the five regions. Neither is a real contradiction.

questions_answered.question: What proof is there that this team has done this venue before?
questions_answered.evidence: None. No past weddings, no couple reviews, no named venue they have worked with, no numbers of weddings planned. Every image is a scenic or generic placeholder. The only 'stories' are celebrity weddings in the Trending row.

questions_answered.question: Why book through you and not the venue directly?
questions_answered.evidence: 'Your advisor is your one contact at Wedded Concierge, instead of one conversation per venue. They walk you through the exact route to marry legally for your nationality and check each venue contract before you sign.' That is a reason. But what it costs me to use them is never stated, and 'Wedded Privileges' is a blank.

questions_answered.question: What happens if something goes wrong on the day?
questions_answered.evidence: Only 'An on-the-day coordinator' in a list of things a weekend 'can include'. The page lists heat waves, wildfire risk June to September, rain October to February and state events cancelling palace bookings, then says nothing about a backup plan, who handles it, or who pays.

objections_triggered.objection: From price with no inclusions list means hidden costs
objections_triggered.triggered_by: No price at all, plus 'There is no set Portugal package' and a weekend list that 'can include' an on-the-day coordinator. The concierge's own fee is never mentioned.
'plans with you from the first enquiry to the last dance' with no evidence of a single wedding planned in Portugal. Trending row of celebrity weddings in place of their own work.

objections_triggered.objection: Inconsistent numbers (capacity or rooms differ in two places)
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Not triggered. Regions, airports, heritage venues and legal timings all match. Only the 'symbolic' versus 'civil marriage in religious form' wording is slightly loose.
'Build a guest website in Wonderland Studio ... Start for free' and 'Wedded Privileges ... your advisor explains what the programme offers'
'state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra' and 'wildfire risk is highest from June to September' with no plan B stated

trust_signals_noticed: Named official sources with links (IRN, Justica, GOV.UK, Smartraveller, US Embassy, Australian Embassy) and 'checked October 2026'
Downsides admitted: Monserrate roof works until Q1 2027, state events can cancel palace bookings, heat waves and wildfire risk
Venue contract checklist naming buy-out, per-guest minimums, unfilled rooms and VAT
No superlatives and no urgency tactics
Honest that a symbolic ceremony is not a legal marriage
turn_offs_noticed: 'What a Wedding in Portugal Costs' heading with no figures under it
'Includes' in a heading over a list that only 'can include'
'Start for free' Wonderland Studio plug in the middle of the page
'Trending row' of celebrity wedding links, Ronaldo twice, label looks unfinished
Region and Portugal-highlights content repeated two or three times, lots of scroll before anything about the service itself

images.stopped_me: None really, they are placeholders. The captions with real detail, like 'Monserrate's lawns and arches, Sintra. Palace roof works run until the first quarter of 2027', were the only image areas I actually read.
felt_generic_or_stock: wedded-advisor-planning-with-couple.jpg: sounds like a stock shot of smiling people at a laptop, which is exactly the kind of thing that proves nothing
quinta-stone-staircase-couple-portugal.jpg and quinta-long-dinner-table-portuguese-wine.jpg: generic 'pretty wedding' filler unless these are their own events, and nothing says they are
fado-guitar-portugal.jpg and azulejo-tile-wall-detail-portugal.jpg: tourism board imagery
images.missing: Any photo labelled as a wedding this team actually planned, at a named venue. That would have been proof.

emotional_response.overall: Grudging respect for the homework on legal paperwork, then irritation that the money and the proof are exactly the two things left out.
emotional_response.fear_of_hidden_costs: Raised, not settled. They tell me where hidden costs hide in a venue contract but not what their own service costs.
emotional_response.fear_of_upsell: Raised by 'Start for free' and the vague 'programme'.

payload.decision_reason: I am deciding this week and I need to compare like for like. This page gives me no from price, no inclusions or exclusions for anything they sell, nothing on what the advisor costs, and zero proof they have ever run a wedding in Portugal. The facts are consistent and well sourced, so I might come back to the legal section as a reference, but my threshold is no unanswered cost question and every cost question here is unanswered. The other tabs at least give me a number to argue with.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Honestly the legal bit is better than anyone else's, I'll give them that. But I scrolled the whole thing and there's a heading literally called 'What a Wedding in Portugal Costs' with no cost in it. What's the catch? Is the advisor free, or are they taking a cut from the venue? Then there's a 'Start for free' button for some website builder, a 'privileges programme' they won't describe, and a 'Trending row' with Ronaldo's wedding twice. Not one wedding they've actually done. Why would I hand my details over just to be told the price on a call?
